• Rolling Plan in India was started in 1978__.
 
• The rolling plan concept was coined by** Gunnar Myrdal**.
 
• This plan was rejected again by the Indian National Congress government when it came to power in 1980 and a new sixth plan was made.
 
• The main advantage of the rolling plans is that they are flexible.
 
• The Rolling Plan is a plan in which every year the performance of the plan is assessed and a new plan is made next year based on this assessment.
 
• Thus, both the allocation and targets are revised during this plan.
 
• **In India, the Janta Government terminated the fifth five-year plan in 1977-78 and launched its own sixth five-year plan for the period 1978-83 and called it a Rolling Plan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
 

 Five-year plan
 
 
Time Period

 
 Comment

 1951-56
 During the initial years of independence, the economy was facing the problem of large-scale foodgrains import (1951) and there was the pressure of price rise. In the plan, the highest priority was given to agriculture including irrigation and power projects. 

 

 
 
 

 Second Plan
 1956-61
 The plan period was 1956–61. The plan laid emphasis on rapid industrialization with a focus on heavy industries and capital goods. The architect of this plan was Professor Mahalanobis. 
 
 

 Third Plan
 1961-65
 This plan incorporated the development of agriculture as one of the objectives of planning in India. It also for the first time, considered the aim of balanced, regional development.  Fourth Plan
 1969-74
 The Plan was based on the Gadgil strategy (named after Dhananjay Ramchandra Gadgil, who was a social scientist who had helped in determining the allocation of central assistance for state plans in India.). There was a focus on the ideas of growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance. This plan led to the beginning of the politicisation of planning in India. questions.question: A boat can go 40 km downstream and 25 km upstream in 7 hours 30 minutes. It can go 48 km downstream and 36 km upstream in 10 hours. What is the speed (in km/h) of the boat in still water?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given time equations: 40/D + 25/U = 7.5 and 48/D + 36/U = 10.

Multiply the first by 6 and the second by 5: 240/D + 150/U = 45 and 240/D + 180/U = 50.

Subtracting yields: 30/U = 5 ⇒ U = 6 km/h. Substituting U back gives D = 12 km/h.

Speed in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/h.**

Case 2: Downstream distance = 48 km, Upstream distance = 36 km, Total time = 10 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Speed of boat in still water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9626c507ec6d6ba68d11adba02e6430a5c699e4f307d589ddda0802fd86024d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let downstream speed be D km/h and upstream speed be U km/h.

⇒ From Case 1: 40/D + 25/U = 15/2 ... (i)

⇒ From Case 2: 48/D + 36/U = 10 ... (ii)

⇒ Multiply equation (i) by 6 and equation (ii) by 5 to equalize the D terms:

⇒ 240/D + 150/U = 45 ... (iii)

⇒ 240/D + 180/U = 50 ... (iv)

⇒ Subtracting (iii) from (iv): 30/U = 5 ⇒ U = 6 km/h

⇒ Substitute U = 6 in equation (i): 40/D + 25/6 = 15/2

⇒ 40/D = 15/2 − 25/6 = 45/6 − 25/6 = 20/6 = 10/3

⇒ D = (40 × 3) ÷ 10 = 12 km/h

⇒ Speed of boat in still water = (D + U) ÷ 2 = (12 + 6) ÷ 2 = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/h.**

questions.question: Find the largest number which completely divides 24, 56 and 96.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **largest number** that divides given numbers, find the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

Check the difference between the closest numbers: 56 − 24 = 32 and 96 − 56 = 40.

The HCF must be a factor of the difference (40 − 32 = 8).

Check if 8 divides 24, 56, and 96: 24/8=3, 56/8=7, 96/8=12. All are divisible.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Prime factorization of 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 56 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 7 = 2³ × 7¹

⇒ Prime factorization of 96 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2⁵ × 3¹

⇒ HCF = Product of lowest powers of common prime factors

⇒ HCF = 2³ = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the **greatest divisor** that divides two or more integers without a remainder.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **smallest positive integer** that is divisible by each of the given numbers.

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers a and b, **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**.</p

• Despite- Used to link two contrasting ideas or show that one fact makes the other fact surprising.
 
 
• *Example: Despite the rain, we enjoyed the festival.*
 
 
 
• In fact- Used **to emphasize the truth of an assertion**, especially one contrary to what might be expected or what has been asserted.
 
 
• *Example: We've had a pretty bad time while you were away. In fact, we very nearly split up this time. *
 
 
 
• As a result- **Used as a conjunctive adverbial phrase** to indicate cause-and-effect relationships.
 
 
• *Example: He sprained his wrist and, as a result, he will not be playing in the tournament. *
